facts: SR-004 is described as a truncated-cone shape in sub-bottom cross-section.
Upper wall slopes are approximately 5-7 degrees.
Lower wall slopes are approximately 18-20 degrees.
The upper slope is gentler in the northeastern half.
Sedimentary layers are reported as sharply truncated in the sub-bottom profile.
Seismic pockmark profiles can be U- or V-shaped and abruptly interrupt shallow sediment reflections.
Some pockmarks have flat bottoms and explicitly resemble a truncated cone.
Very steep slopes and narrow floors occur in some pockmarks.
Acoustic turbid zones occur below pockmark floors and are interpreted as gas-bearing sediment / continuing gas supply.
process_control.source: Geophysical and Geochemical Exploration of the Pockmark Field in the Gulf of Patras: New Insights on Formation, Growth and Activity, Applied Sciences 13 (2023) 10449

killer_prediction.fluid_escape: truncated-cone bowl should connect downward to ATZ/acoustic blanking, bright reflectors, a chimney/pipe and/or fault plumbing
killer_prediction.impact: bowl should overlie a deep excavation/fracture architecture with impact-derived breccia/shock evidence rather than terminate as a shallow gas-fed collapse
